Generate a population with uniformly distributed ages

Source: R/generate_uniform_population.R
generate_uniform_population.Rd

Create a starter population with independent uniformly distributed ages, randomly assigned sex, unknown parents, and no unions.

Usage

generate_uniform_population(
  size,
  max_age = 70,
  end_time = 0,
  min_age = 0,
  female_probability = 0.5,
  groups = NULL
)

Arguments

size

Number of living persons, a nonnegative whole number.

max_age

Maximum initial age in years, finite and nonnegative.

end_time

Reference time in years, finite. Birth times are this value minus the sampled ages. Defaults to a relative time origin of zero.

min_age

Minimum initial age in years, finite and nonnegative, and no greater than max_age. Defaults to zero.

female_probability

Probability of assigning sex "f" (female). The other sex value is "m" (male).

groups

Optional group dimensions to sample, independently of age and sex. Either a named list with one named numeric vector of weights per dimension (categories as names; dimensions are drawn independently), or a data frame with one column per dimension and a numeric weight column, giving the joint distribution of category combinations. Weights are finite and nonnegative with at least one positive value, and are normalized. NULL (the default) adds no groups.

Value

A validated hammel_population object.

Details

Ages are sample from the uniform distribution between min_age and max_age and only the living population is generated. This population will have no father or mother ids. Sex and group categories follow their supplied probabilities.

The generated population will not have a realistic age distribution. Typically, users will run a "burn in" simulation to produce a more realistic population distribution and kinship history for the desired simulation.

The end_time for the population will define the starting point for the simulation. By default, this value is set to zero so that time is measured since the beginning of the simulation. This means that birth times for the existing population will be negative. Users who are drawing from input data with time increments from real calendar time, should reset this starting value as appropriate.

If the groups argument is used, the population declares each dimension with group() defaults, except that its categories are those given, in order:

  • the weights' names

  • each dimension's values in order of first appearance in the table's rows.

The first is the reference category, and zero-weight categories are declared, allowing for groups that may emerge later. set_groups() can replace that declaration; categories it omits are kept.

Examples

set.seed(42)

# generate 50000 people with a maximum age of 50
population <- generate_uniform_population(size = 50000, max_age = 50)

# generate a population divided by race and region, with unequal division
# of race by region
region_race_dist <- tibble::tribble(
  ~race, ~region, ~weight,
 "W",   "NE",    0.145,
 "W",   "MW",    0.190,
 "W",   "S",     0.257,
 "W",   "W",     0.152,
 "B",   "NE",    0.022,
 "B",   "MW",    0.023,
 "B",   "S",     0.067,
 "B",   "W",     0.019,
 "O",   "NE",    0.021,
 "O",   "MW",    0.014,
 "O",   "S",     0.030,
 "O",   "W",     0.060,
)
population <- generate_uniform_population(50000, groups = region_race_dist)
prop.table(table(population$persons$race, population$persons$region))
#>    
#>          MW      NE       S       W
#>   B 0.02316 0.02238 0.06700 0.01818
#>   O 0.01408 0.02154 0.03044 0.05972
#>   W 0.18980 0.14254 0.25886 0.15230
